To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
macrophages exposed to E coli are able to stimulate lymphocytes to proliferate in the absence of the antigen.
macrophages are required as accessory cells in the in vitro response of human lymphocytes to E. coli, and that the response of T cells is antigen specific while that of B cells is polyclonal.
Macrophages are required as accessory cells in the response of both T and of B cells to a clinically relevant bacterial antigen (E Coli).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of human lymphocytes, macrophages and bacterial antigens in vitro.
the role of the macrophage as an accessory cell in the immune response to bacterial antigen.
the role of the macrophage as an accessory cell in the response of T cells and B cells to a bacterial antigen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
E. coli is a clinically relevant antigen which is capable of stimulating human lymphocytes.
macrophages are required to present antigen to lymphocytes.
macrophages are required as accessory cells in the E coli induced response of both T and polyclonal B lymphocytes, but the macrophage-lymphoocyte interaction is not antigen specific.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
macrophages are required as accessory cells in the E coli induced polyclonal B-cell and antigen specific T cell proliferative response.
E. coli antigen is taken up by macrophages, processed and presented to T cells, and that the macrophages can also act as accessory cells to B cells.
the interaction of human lymphocytes and macrophages is a highly regulated process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
macrophage-lymphocytes interaction is important in bacterial infection.
the macrophage is a critical cell for lymphocyte activation in response to a particulate bacterial antigen.
the interaction of lymphocytes with macrophages in the context of bacterial infection is a highly regulated process that is controlled in time and space.
